Dave Mitchell and Dudley Gordon both reached the final of the 880 where Dave was narrowly beaten by Haith of the Valley. In the mile John Thresher ran particularly well to gain third place in 4:26.0 behind Pegley and Darchambaud (S.L.H.) 4:23.0 and finish in front of Mal Robinson.

When the Pompey runner moved away it seemed Chas. was to have one of those days , but when Haith (T.V.H.)and later White (Woodford) caught up it seemed to act as a tonic and he stayed with them to the end, where with a typical final flourish he kept us in third place, only thirty secs. down on Pompey.
Charlie Walker, once again beginning to show his old form, swept into the lead; only to be passed by Haith of T.V.H. who had moved up from 13th.

International Haith in the Melbourne Trophy 3,000 m. at Tooting. He beat several established stars to clock 8:21, a new club best performance.

Haith of T.V.H. caught and passed Newell by the time Tooting Bec Station was reached, but Pat kept his head and in the end took us up to third position, 36 secs, behind the leaders; an excellent effort.

Ron had a tremendous tussle with Haith (T.V.H) but the Valley star was in great form and took his club ahead of us. However, Ron gained three further places and showing all of his old fire and determination brought us to the change-over in 6th position.
John Thresher held his position on Stage 5 but we were now 1 min.43secs. behind the new leaders T.V.H. who had taken the lead, thanks to a fine run by Haith.
On this occasion, however, Barry's legs did the chasing and Haith of T.V.H. was the main sufferer. His time of 18:30 gave John Thresher a send-off in 7th position.
Unfortunately we had already lost Bob Farley at 3½ miles---Bob suffering his 2nd successive disqualification in "Opens". Haith and J.

Herring (Blackheath) set a tremendously fast pace right from the start with North and Haith (TVH) at his shoulder. Thresher was not so well away and had to make a great effort for 1½ miles to close with the leaders.

Meanwhile, back on the by-pass, Haith (Camb.H.) had caught Clive to make the team points level, though this was unknown to either of them. A tremendous tussle developed going into Copse but the hill was kind to the Belgravian and could offer nothing but sickness to the Cambridge man.
